pr.title: Call a pull request's unresolved threads findings, and count none on its row
pr.head: 10d2a0baa7a4e4644beaae2a429439053dfa3c3e

summary: Projector's panel, the list above the Claude Code prompt, gives each pull request one row: its number, a state word such as findings or changes, its title, and then notes that name every other state that applies. Clicking a row opens its drawer, and while the drawer is open the row spells each hold out in full, such as checks failing for failing and changes requested for changes. A hold is one of the states that keeps a pull request from merging: a conflict, failing checks, a change request, or unresolved review threads.

Before this change, the state for unresolved review threads was called threads, and its spelled-out form was the thread count, such as 1 thread. So an open row put a count back on the row, and when threads was already the row's state word, the open row repeated it as a note. The drawer's file lines already count each file's threads, so the count said nothing new.

Now the state is called findings, Projector's word for an unresolved review thread, which the watch daemon's FINDING events already use. It has no longer form: the row names it as the note findings only when another hold took the state word, with the drawer open or closed, and never counts it. checks failing and changes requested still spell themselves out in an open drawer. The drawer's file lines count each file's findings, such as + src/a.ts 2 findings.

groups.title: The row's notes stop counting findings
groups.kicker: How each hold becomes a note, and the tests that pin it
intro: HOLDS lists the holds in the order the state word takes them. Each entry has a status, the short word, and an optional phrase, the spelled-out form an open drawer shows. notesOf turns the holds that apply into the row's notes, skipping the one that is already the state word unless the drawer is open and the hold has a phrase.

The change makes phrase a plain string, drops the phrase of the hold for unresolved threads, and renames that hold's word from threads to findings. A hold without a phrase now always shows its short word. conflict also has no phrase, and stays out of the notes because it is first in HOLDS: whenever it applies, it is the state word.

checks.text: The row's state word and its color come from rowState, which reads only status and color, so the colors are unchanged. The review traced every reader of HOLDS, and findingCount has only the drawer's file lines as its caller.

files.note: The panel's module. The hold for unresolved threads is renamed findings and loses its count, and notesOf spells a hold out only when it has a phrase.

checks.text: For failing and changes, open or closed, the notes give the same text as at the base. For findings, they give the word only when another hold is the state word. The review walked each case, and claude plugin test . passed.
With isNoted gone, a conflict still never shows as a note. It is the first hold, so it is the state word whenever it applies, and with no phrase status !== shown keeps it out, open or closed.

files.note: The tests follow the new word and expect no count on the row, open or closed.

checks.text: This comment says the file counts add up to the row's own count of threads, and the comment at line 3975 says the yellow number matches the row's count. No row shows a count any more, so both comments misstate the code. The review asks for both to be reworded.
